title: Optimize quant kernels: INT8/FP8 smoothquant + dequant-fusion; KV cache & continuous-batching improvements
author: Aria Patel
release_notes: Optimized INT8/FP8 quantized kernels with smoothquant support and dequant-fusion; improved KV cache allocation/copy paths and continuous batching heuristics. Feature-flagged rollout: redwood.quant.v2. Expect ~+20% throughput and reduced p99 for short-sequence LLM workloads.
description:
Context: Customers running quantized LLMs (INT8/FP8 with SmoothQuant) have been asking for lower p99 and higher sustained throughput on short to medium sequence lengths. The current runtime suffered extra dequant/quant copies and missed opportunities for fusing dequant with GEMM kernels, causing higher memory traffic and suboptimal kernel utilization. This PR implements a fused dequant+matmul execution path, SmoothQuant-aware scaling in the kernel, KV-cache copy/eviction optimizations, and continuous-batching heuristic updates to reduce tail latency. Changes are behind a feature flag (redwood.quant.v2) and covered by unit+perf tests.

This description includes: motivation, approach, and rollout plan. Checklist: - [x] Implement fused dequant+GEMM kernels for common shapes - [x] Add SmoothQuant scaling support to kernel prologue - [x] Update scheduler to prefer fused path when model+shape compatible - [x] Reduce KV cache memcpy by sharded updates and early allocation - [x] Improve continuous-batching heuristics to microbatch short requests - [x] Add unit, integration and perf tests + benchmarks - [x] Add docs and feature-flag gating

Motivation: Fusion reduces memory bandwidth and avoids repeated convert/from-fp ops on the hot path. For small batch/short-seq workloads the overhead of separate dequant stages dominated latency; fusing eliminates that. SmoothQuant requires per-channel scaling in kernel prologue — added a small precompute path that is cheap at runtime and amortized across tokens.

Approach: - Implemented quant::fused_dequant_gemm (specialized for INT8 and FP8 input variants) which performs dequant on-the-fly and computes matmul in a single kernel. - Added fast path dispatch in the runtime that selects fused kernel when (model uses SmoothQuant OR model quantized) AND sequence_len <= 256 AND batch_size <= 8 (configurable). - KV cache: avoid full-row memcpy for cache hits by maintaining sharded slab-backed buffers and performing incremental writes on append. - Batcher updates: added microbatching loop that splits incoming requests when latency SLOs are tight and blends with continuous batcher so throughput isn't regressed. - Added runtime telemetry for fused-path usage rate and per-kernel token/sec metrics.

Benchmarks (summary): Llama-2-7B quantized (INT8, smoothquant pipeline) on p4d: - Throughput: +22% sustained tokens/sec for mixed-size workloads - P50 latency: -12% - P99 latency: -18% (short sequences <=128 tokens) - Memory traffic reduced ~30% on hot GEMM paths

Testing: Unit tests for kernel correctness across INT8/FP8/smoothquant combos; integration tests with KV cache enabled; perf harness run recorded in /bench/perf/2024-11-10/quant-fusion.

Rollout: Feature-flag redwood.quant.v2=false by default. Staged rollout to Dedicated clusters first, then Hosted. Observability: added dashboards and alerts for fused-path error rate and token/sec regressions. If regressions detected, runtime falls back to legacy path automatically.

Notes/links: Linear tickets ENG-9421 (quant fusion design), ENG-9582 (batcher heuristics). Related PRs: pr-21487, pr-218401, pr-246789 (previous quant tuning work).

review_comments: Liam Chen: Nice work. Can you quantify accuracy impact of SmoothQuant+dequant fusion? We need a small table comparing logits / perplexity vs baseline.
Aria Patel: Added a small accuracy check in tests/quant/accuracy_smootquant.md and included the summary in the perf run. No measurable regression on validation prompts (within noise).
Omar Khalid: kvcache changes look good but I worry about fragmentation under heavy eviction. How reversible is this rollout?

Aria Patel: Eviction policy unchanged; we use slab-backed allocations per-shard. If we see fragmentation we can revert by disabling redwood.quant.v2 or switching kvcache.experimental=false. Added a canary metric 'kvcache.fragmentation_pct' to aid rollback decisions.
